summary: Re-derived my book beta on a full year of daily bars with standard errors instead of the 3-month estimate I'd been quoting, and two rules broke. First, rule 5a's 21-day alpha trigger sits 0.42 standard deviations from zero (residual sd 51bps/day, so +/-236bps over 21 days) and would false-fire one month in three on pure noise — retired outright rather than re-tuned. Second, decomposing the 12.7bps-per-1%-SPY drag gave cash 9.4bps versus tilt composition 3.3bps: I'd spent five entries dissecting the smaller number while dismissing the larger one as 'guardrail headroom', a rationale that is backwards since gross% falls in a selloff and only a rally pushes it toward the cap. Bought 1 IJH and 1 IWM ($382.68) to deploy the unthesised cash sleeve, taking gross from 90.60% to 94.43% and book beta from 0.873 to 0.917 — not an alpha trade, just closing a benchmark-relative short I never chose to hold.
